newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Zeneca gets warning from U.S. FDA.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Zeneca gets warning from U.S. FDA.

text.p: Shares in British drugs company Zeneca Group Plc tumbled on Friday following news that the U.S. Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) had issued a warning to the company following an inspection at one of Zeneca's plants in northwest England.

The FDA said it would not recommend approval of any new applications which list Zeneca as the manufacturer of sterile pharmaceuticals until the problems identified at its Macclesfield plant had been resolved.
The sterile manufacturing area subject to the FDA inspection is a sophisticated plant responsible exclusively for a cancer treatment called Zoladex.
The shares fell by as much as two and a half percent or 49-1/2 pence to 17.89 pounds, in response to the news on Friday.

"The concerns about the FDA not allowing any new injectable products are overdone," said Kevin Wilson, pharmaceutical analyst at Salomon Brothers. "None of the products that are important to Zeneca in the new product stream are of this type, or are manufactured at this base," he added.

Zeneca said the safety and efficacy of Zolidex itself, which has been manufactured at Macclesfield for 11 years, is not under investigation. The company said the manufacture, supply, and use of the drug is unaffected by the FDA's warning.
Zeneca also said it was seeking to resolve the matter quickly and had already met with FDA officials since being notified of the warning on February 20.
"We are confident of resolving the issue and we are continuing to supply out of Macclesfield," a company spokesman said.
Salomon's Wilson said the news had not altered his perspective on the company's short-term prospects.
"This sort of thing is not common, but it does happen from time to time with such complex manufacturing processes."
"The important thing is there is no hint of any interruption to supply, manufacturing is continuing as normal," Wilson said.
The company produces other anti-cancer and cardiovascular drugs at the same plant.
Analysts said that the sharp fall in the company's share-price was a knee-jerk reaction but had perhaps been overdone.
"I still think the shares are attractive, and this setback could represent a good buying opportunity," Wilson said.
Last week, shares in the company would have cost up to 18.95-1/2 pounds.
